skill.name: pdb-database
skill.description: Search and retrieve RCSB Protein Data Bank structures, metadata, sequence matches, and coordinate files for structural biology workflows.

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, public RCSB API examples, safe local downloads, or a report artifact. No prompt injection, credential access, data exfiltration, or malicious command execution was found. A low-severity semantic concern remains because the skill asks the assistant to promote the author's hosted K-Dense Web platform.

remediation.issue: Promotional steering appears inside runtime skill instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the K-Dense Web promotion or move it to clearly labeled marketplace metadata outside the skill prompt.

remediation.issue: The API reference includes a subprocess curl debugging example.
remediation.suggestion: Use the RCSB Python client or requests for the example to avoid encouraging external command execution.

remediation.issue: Download helpers write files from user-oriented identifiers.
remediation.suggestion: Validate PDB IDs, allowed formats, and output directories before saving downloaded structure files.

content.value_statement: Structural biology work needs reliable access to protein and nucleic acid structures. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code search RCSB PDB and retrieve structure data.
actual_capabilities: Search RCSB PDB by text, organism, resolution, method, ligand, or other attributes.
Run sequence similarity searches with amino acid, DNA, or RNA sequences.
Find structures by 3D similarity using RCSB structure search concepts.
Retrieve entry, entity, assembly, and experimental metadata through RCSB APIs.
Download PDB, mmCIF, BinaryCIF, assembly, FASTA, and structure factor files.
Plan batch retrieval workflows with rate limiting and caching guidance.
limitations: Requires internet access to public RCSB PDB endpoints.
Results depend on current RCSB API availability and rate limits.
Downloaded coordinates need external viewers or libraries for detailed analysis.
Examples are guidance; users must validate biological interpretation independently.

use_cases.title: Find Ligand-Bound Targets
use_cases.description: Search for protein-ligand structures, compare resolution, and shortlist entries for drug discovery analysis.

use_cases.title: Select Modeling Templates
use_cases.description: Find homologous structures and compare sequence identity, coverage, organism, and structure quality.

use_cases.title: Prepare Teaching Examples
use_cases.description: Retrieve well-known structures and metadata for molecular visualization, assignments, and classroom discussion.

prompt_templates.title: Find One Structure
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner search for a known protein
prompt_templates.prompt: Search RCSB PDB for hemoglobin. Return the best PDB IDs, methods, resolutions, and short titles.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Structure Quality
prompt_templates.scenario: Filter entries by method and resolution
prompt_templates.prompt: Find human kinase structures with resolution better than 2.0 Angstroms. Summarize organism, method, ligand presence, and suitability.

prompt_templates.title: Search By Sequence
prompt_templates.scenario: Find homologous structures from a sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this protein sequence to find similar PDB entries: [paste sequence]. Rank results by identity, coverage, and experimental quality.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A Batch Retrieval
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a rate-limited plan to download mmCIF files and metadata for these PDB IDs: [list IDs]. Include validation steps.

output_examples.input: Find the best human hemoglobin structure.
output: Use mmCIF for modern parsing and PDB format for legacy tools.
The result set should include kinase entries with ATP or related ligands.
Compare resolution, organism, chain identifiers, ligand identifiers, and experimental method.
Download coordinate files only for shortlisted entries.
Use a small batch with a delay between requests.
Save mmCIF files and entry metadata together for reproducibility.
Check each response for missing or obsolete identifiers.

best_practices: Start with Search API filters before downloading coordinate files.
Use small batches with delays and cache repeated metadata requests.
Record PDB IDs, file formats, and query criteria for reproducible analysis.
anti_patterns: Do not download large result sets before narrowing the search.
Do not ignore HTTP errors, obsolete identifiers, or empty API responses.
Do not treat structural matches as biological conclusions without review.

faq.question: What database does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses public RCSB Protein Data Bank APIs and RCSB file download endpoints.

faq.question: Can it download coordinate files?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents PDB, mmCIF, BinaryCIF, biological assembly, FASTA, and structure factor downloads.

faq.question: Does it require an API key?
faq.answer: The documented RCSB PDB public endpoints generally do not require an API key. Users still need to respect rate limits.

faq.question: Can it search by protein sequence?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes sequence similarity workflows for protein, DNA, and RNA searches.

faq.question: Can it compare structure quality?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide searches by resolution, experimental method, organism, release date, and related metadata.

faq.question: Does it perform molecular analysis itself?
faq.answer: No. It retrieves data and suggests workflows. Detailed geometry analysis needs tools such as BioPython or molecular viewers.
